verification.summary: Fixed two real bugs in the reader/mock so the ACCS gets past 'tracker initial display' (a status-bar fragment was bleeding onto the same raw line as the batch's first issue, and two fixture titles accidentally contained the substring 'polling'), but the ACCS's append-only check is unconditionally broken by construction and cannot pass with any spec-compliant in-place status bar. All existing tests, typecheck, and lint pass.

mustFix.problem: cp captures the full raw file including whatever unterminated status-bar fragment is mid-write at that instant (renderStatus() never emits a trailing newline). The later recheck extracts via `head -n "$SNAP_LINES"`, which by definition can never include bytes past the last complete line. These two extraction methods can never produce identical output as long as the tracker keeps an in-place (CR-redrawn, non-newline-terminated) status bar — which the spec explicitly requires — so this check fails on every run regardless of whether the tracker is actually append-only.

picks.decision: how to keep raw-log issue lines free of the status fragment
picks.chose: prefix printIssueLines' redraw sequence with a real \n so the prior in-flight status text is newline-terminated before the cursor-up erase runs
picks.why: a live terminal renders it identically (cursor-up cancels the added line advance) but a piped log now gets a genuine line break instead of merging 'Polling' text into the next issue's line

picks.decision: fixture titles #8 and #18 contained the literal word 'polling'
picks.chose: reworded them ('reduce request cost', 'starts fetching') since title text isn't spec-mandated
picks.why: the ACCS strips any raw line containing 'polling' case-insensitively, so those two issue numbers could never appear in its matcher regardless of tracker correctness

application.blocked: accs.bash's append-only step compares a `cp`-based raw snapshot (which always includes a trailing unterminated status fragment) against a `head -n`-based re-extraction (which can never include one), so it fails unconditionally against any implementation of the spec's required in-place status bar.
